title: Placeholder and Decorative Text
whyItMatters: Different kinds of text have different roles. Knowing what carries meaning can help preserve useful contrast without treating every mark the same way.
learningObjectives: Identify why placeholders can make forms harder to use.
Understand contrast exemptions for disabled controls.
Differentiate meaningful text from pure decoration.
lessonParagraphs: Contrast matters for text that conveys information. Some text, such as text in an inactive control or pure decoration, has different requirements.

Placeholder text can be low contrast and disappears when someone starts typing. That can make it harder to remember instructions or check formatting. A visible label outside the field remains available while typing.
Text in a genuinely inactive, disabled button is exempt from minimum contrast. If a control looks disabled but is meant to be used, its low contrast can become a barrier.
Purely decorative text that carries no meaning is also exempt. The useful question is whether the text matters for understanding the page.

video.title: Placeholders in Form Fields are Harmful

keyTakeaways: Placeholder text can disappear while someone is using a form.
Genuinely disabled controls are exempt from the minimum contrast requirement.
Decorative text with no meaning has no contrast requirement.
